content.text: {"id": "mm5739a1", "data_focus": {"v": "yes", "ev": [{"loc": "summary", "q": "the prevalence of disability among U.S. adults ranged from 11.6% among Asians to 29.9% among AI/ANs"}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Overall, adults with a disability were less likely to report excellent or very good health (27.2% versus 60.2%; p<0.01)"}]}, "outcome_types": [{"v": "binary/categorical", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "an estimated 19.9% of the total U.S. population aged > 18 years"}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Nearly 60% of white, Asian, and Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander respondents"}]}], "analytic_depth": [{"v": "summary", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "During 2004 -- 2006, an estimated 19.9% of the total U.S. population aged > 18 years"}]}, {"v": "comparison", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "adults with a disability were less likely to report excellent or very good health (27.2% versus 60.2%; p<0.01)"}]}, {"v": "stratified/adjusted", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "This analysis also determined that the difference in self-rated fair or poor health between persons with and without disabilities varied by race/ethnicity."}, {"loc": "table 1", "q": "Age adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population."}]}], "study_design": [{"v": "cross-sectional", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "because of the cross-sectional nature of the data, inferring any direction of causality between disability and fair or poor health is not possible"}]}], "methods_quotes": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Prevalence estimates were weighted and age adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Prevalence estimates and standard errors were obtained using statistical software to account for the complex sampling design."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Chi-square tests were used to compare self-rated health status between racial/ethnic populations and by disability status."}], "confidence": "high", "uncertain_fields": []}
